flashcard_questions.q: Which letter pattern describes rondo form?
What are the contrasting sections between returns of the rondo theme called?
In which key does the A section of a rondo usually return?
Which Mozart work is named as an example of rondo form?
flashcard_questions.a: The second movement of Eine Kleine Nachtmusik.

flashcard_questions.q: How is theme and variation form labelled?
flashcard_questions.a: A, then A1, A2, A3 for each new variation.

flashcard_questions.q: What must stay recognisable through every variation?

flashcard_questions.a: Playing the theme in quicker note values.
Playing the theme in slower note values.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Haydn symphony is a famous example of theme and variations?
flashcard_questions.a: Symphony No. 94 in G major, the Surprise.

flashcard_questions.q: Which accompaniment style does an Alberti bass use?

flashcard_questions.a: The same music repeated for every verse with different words.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Schubert song is named as an example of strophic form?
Which Schubert song is named as a through-composed example?

flashcard_questions.a: The use of notes from outside the main key, moving in semitones.

flashcard_questions.q: How do rondo episodes differ from the sections of a theme and variations?
flashcard_questions.a: Episodes are completely new ideas; variations transform the original theme.

notes: 15 cards: 4 rondo cards (letter pattern, episodes, tonic return, Mozart example), 6 variation cards (labelling, recognisable theme, diminution, augmentation, Haydn example, Alberti bass), 3 strophic and through-composed cards with their named Schubert songs, 1 term card (chromaticism) and 1 misconception card separating episodes from variations. Named works carry the example-to-feature load. Dropped the long list of variation techniques, which would only make enumeration answers.
